name: Troy Jackson

issue_poll.name: Fox News Maine polls (June 23-27 and Aug 6-10, 2026), combined with NYT/Siena Maine polls (Sept 15-22; Oct 27-Nov 1, 2026), AARP Maine (Sept 20-22), CNN/SSRS (Aug 31-Sept 6) and UMass Lowell (Aug 28-Sept 14)
issue_poll.note: No single 2026 Maine poll with a full published ranking was reachable. Base order from Fox News June 'most important issue to your Senate vote' (inflation 30%, political divisions 19%, healthcare 17%, immigration 14%; then unemployment, Iran, abortion, crime unquantified), with August Fox (inflation ~1/3, immigration 18%). NYT/Siena final (Oct 27-Nov 1) and Sept polls list economy first (21%) and inflation/cost of living (12%) separately, so both are kept. 'Political divisions' and 'which party controls Congress' dropped as not vote-testable; 'threats to democracy' (AARP #2, CNN top-2) kept as Democracy and elections. Energy costs and AI data centers added from UMass Lowell (61% blame Iran war for fuel/utility prices; 76% oppose local data center) and NYT/Siena (66% oppose data centers). Ranks 5-10 are approximate.

issues.detail: Federal government should do more to lower prices for health care, housing, groceries and heat; no specific measure.
Raise the federal minimum wage; expand family and medical leave; strengthen union rights. No figures given.
Enact Medicare for All (universal government health insurance covering everyone).
Abolish ICE; oppose any additional ICE funding.
Get dark money out of politics (campaign finance reform); restore congressional oversight of the executive.
Cut off congressional funding for the Iran war and bring troops home; no U.S. military aid to Israel.
Restore and expand a federal statutory right to abortion.
Prioritize large clean energy projects and electrification, including Northern Maine onshore wind and transmission; no target.
Prevent data centers from raising residents' electric and water rates; more federal AI guardrails.

plan_caveats: Issue ranking is a combination of partial poll releases; no single poll with a full ranked list was accessible (Marist and NYT/Siena crosstabs not reachable). Ranks 5-10 are approximate.

Campaign 'Priorities' and 'Troy at a Glance' pages could not be fetched; ratings rely on campaign press releases, debate coverage and interviews. Jackson became nominee only on July 25, 2026, so his platform is thin.

Abortion rated Concrete on 'restore and expand the federal right to abortion' as a clear end state (federal statutory right); no bill (e.g., WHPA) or filibuster position was named, so a stricter reading would be Partial.
Democracy rated Partial on 'get dark money out of politics'; no specific bill (DISCLOSE Act, constitutional amendment, stock-trading ban) was named.
Also stated but outside the top 10: eliminate the Social Security payroll tax cap and expand benefits (BDN, Oct 8, 2026); oppose Trump tariffs on Canada.
Win as given in task (CBS News projection); not independently confirmed in this research.
